question: Which conversion laws share an owner across formats, and what Markdown reuse contract preserves every partial-prefix result without repeated whole-response work?
trigger: User selected one conversion-boundary review, challenging earlier sequencing and proposing common conversion laws plus incremental Markdown; product audit only.
requirements: Keep the adopted CommonMark/GFM/math/registered-tag dialect and declarative format-mapping direction unless new decisive evidence justifies a separate change.
Schema-valid document admission and context-correct insertion-slice admission with explicit loss; reuse existing Plite schema/fitter authority rather than validating every slice as a full document.

One role-aware semantic safety law across active input/output paths, including custom callbacks, paste and retained DOCX source reuse; permissive loss never authorizes unsafe active output. Literal text and legitimate media resources remain distinguishable.
Common property exposure and honest preservation/loss policy, compared under equal capabilities/defaults/roles rather than requiring identical losses across unequal formats.

Every reused preview equals a fresh full partial parse of the same prefix, including diagnostics/coordinates; grammar and callback dependencies may invalidate earlier output. Completion strictly parses original source.

Parser state belongs to Markdown; consumer cancel/accept/undo remain outside it. Prove non-AI use, configuration validity, aggregate limits and bounded retention before selecting a public reuse contract.
Separate parse, fitting, publication and browser rendering claims; preserve sampling, workload, source identity and missing proof. No unmeasured engine/render win or 3.2-second universal CPU claim.
No product implementation, staging/commit, AI product/prompt redesign, universal AST or full HTML mapping redesign in this assessment.
evidenceReuse: Reconciled prior mapping design, adopted dialect, serialize repair, contextual slice-fitting decision and retained-source execution. Current source probes reproduce property and URL/output differences; preserved safety probe was rerun (56 observations, 10 assertions) and property probe rerun at durable paths. Delegated primary-source comparison pins six local repositories. Streaming evidence compares 1,996 prefixes, preserved identity failures and bounded 10/50 KB timings; source-first Chromium covers only existing editable/static Columns. Historical paste/report claims are not assumed true for the later slice-or-null adapters. Copied original harnesses and selected receipts outside ignored artifacts, without relabeling them new measured runs.
summary: Pursue shared private role-aware safety, property exposure and truthful loss accounting at existing Plate conversion owners; delete property-read inference and unchecked retained-source output bypasses. Reuse Plite fitting/admission and retain format-specific meaning, resources and artifact lifetimes. Pursue dependency-aware Markdown reuse, with previous-result provenance the leading candidate, not an adopted API. Reject unconditional tail-only work and a universal conversion pipeline. Preserve declarative mappings and micromark/MDAST; settle shared D2 contracts before adoption without blocking other declaration simplification on an engine redesign. Restricted 10 KB parsing improves while fitting/publication do not; existing model identity already survives. General identity and 50 KB sampling/Chromium candidate acceptance remain unproven. Recommend cutting unused detached public HTML slice exports under the same current-job rule as Markdown fragments.

reconciliation.question: Which schema-bound construction and property contracts should HTML, Markdown and plain-text feature mappings share without erasing their format semantics?
reconciliation.reason: Pure schema-bound declarations and feature-specific exceptions remain valuable; parser engine replacement does not itself invalidate those contracts.

reconciliation.reason: D2 property exposure needs common ownership and truthful loss accounting before S1 adoption. Preserve declarative construction and mark direction; do not wait for a general incremental engine to simplify unrelated declarations.

reconciliation.reason: Historical browser/media proof remains historical evidence. Current source exposes obfuscated child-URL safety gaps and slice-or-null adapters that discard diagnostics; earlier report/toast behavior is not assumed current.

reconciliation.question: Which document conversion laws should DOCX file import, export and Word paste share, and where must fidelity limits be explicit?
reconciliation.reason: Opaque retained source and fidelity remain real jobs, but exact-source export is not eligible unconditionally under the selected active-output safety law. The probe returns an unsafe original relationship through unchanged-source reuse; no claim of Word execution.

alternatives: Keep/configure current paths: rejected by demonstrated unsafe bypasses, false preservation claims and inconsistent reject severity; UI sanitization alone leaves canonical data and exports unsafe.

Shared private admission/emission core: pursue policy/accounting primitives at existing Plate owners and reuse Plite admission; reject a mandatory universal pipeline/AST because formats own distinct semantics, coordinates, resources and source lifetimes.
Strongest cuts: remove property-read proxies as proof, duplicated loss decisions and unchecked retained-source export eligibility; D2 ownership cannot become blanket preservation.

Block incremental plus joiner deletion: pursue dependency-aware stable reuse with conservative fallback and prefix oracle. Reject unconditional tail-only work; defer deletion of transport grammar/delays until cadence and strict finalization proof.

Previous-result hint versus stream handle: previous is the leading fit for accumulated-source callers, with opaque compiler-owned provenance. Both require validity, immutability/retention and stateful-transform policy; no public API selected by this review.

Retain micromark/MDAST versus engine replacement: keep current matched baseline. Source-supported complexity risks and B4 alone do not justify rewriting the grammar; replacement requires equivalent semantics and complete-operation budgets.

Detached slice symmetry: recommend cutting unused public browser/server parseHtmlSlice, keeping editor slice and standalone document operations. Do not re-add detached Markdown slices solely for symmetry.
Blanket Plite URL validation or recursive sanitization: rejected because neutral model strings, literal text and resource roles differ. Plate format input/output boundaries own role-aware policy.
proofLimits: Audit/prototypes only, no product adoption. Incremental fast path admits only restricted independent plain ASCII paragraphs/ATX headings; rich syntax falls back to full parsing. Broader unchanged parser-object identity fails (181/926), aggregate quota/configuration/closure-state reuse is not established. Ten-KB timings have five alternating pairs; 50 KB has one of five pairs, rich fallback one un-warmed pair. Fitting and publication independently fit and cannot be summed. Existing model/key reuse is headless top-level positional evidence, not React proof. Chromium passed two current Columns modes but did not compare 10/50 KB candidate parse/publish/render or isolate React commits/paint. No native Word, live exploit, complete resource/protocol fuzzing, OS paste or external-consumer census. Arbitrary callback fidelity cannot be inferred from reads. Cloned prior art was source-inspected, not benchmarked.
